intent.raw_query: Patagonia hiking Torres del Paine, $4500, 12 days, December 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through the heart of Torres del Paine National Park. The trail covers approximately 80km and takes you through stunning valleys, glacial lakes, and dramatic granite towers. You'll pass through Valle del Francés, Mirador Las Torres, and the Grey Glacier, experiencing some of the most breathtaking scenery in all of Patagonia.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Base Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Wake before dawn and hike 4-5 hours to the iconic base of the Torres del Paine granite towers. Arriving at sunrise rewards you with golden light illuminating the three towering peaks reflected in the turquoise glacial lagoon below. This is arguably the most photographed and awe-inspiring viewpoint in all of Patagonia and a bucket-list moment for any nature lover.
experiences.location: Mirador Base Las Torres, Eastern Sector

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through icy turquoise waters surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. A guided kayaking tour brings you up close to the 6km-wide glacier face, offering a perspective impossible to achieve on foot. Expert guides provide all equipment and safety briefings, making this an accessible yet thrilling adventure for trekkers looking to diversify their Patagonian experience.

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Condor Watching Trek
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers and towering peaks including Paine Grande and Cerro Espada. This full-day trek is renowned for Andean condor sightings, with the massive birds riding thermal currents above the valley. The trail culminates at Mirador Británico, offering a 360-degree panorama of the park's most spectacular peaks.

experiences.name: Lago Nordenskjöld Shoreline Trek & Guanaco Spotting
experiences.description: Trek along the vivid turquoise shores of Lago Nordenskjöld, one of the most scenic lakes in the park, with the Paine Massif reflected in its glassy waters. This moderate trail is a prime location for spotting wild guanacos, Patagonian foxes, and rheas in their natural habitat. The route connects key sectors of the park and offers constantly changing perspectives of the iconic towers and horns above.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Torres del Paine, Patagonia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 on UA flight. Collect luggage, arrange pre-booked budget transfer or shared shuttle to Puerto Natales (approx. 1.5-2 hrs). Check into Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine area. Grab a light snack from any open convenience store or hotel reception if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Light snack from convenience store or vending machine near accommodation upon arrival — budget ~$5-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Keep a small amount of Chilean Pesos (CLP) on hand for tips and small purchases. Pre-book your shared shuttle in advance to save money. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements for late arrival. Rest well — big hiking days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow morning, head into Puerto Natales town center on foot or by local bus. Visit the Museo Histórico Municipal (free or very low cost) to learn about Patagonian history and culture. Stock up on trail snacks, groceries, and trekking supplies at local supermarkets (Unimarc or Almacén) — far cheaper than park prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Seno Última Esperanza waterfront boardwalk for stunning views of the fjord and surrounding mountains — completely free. Visit the local artisan market for budget souvenirs. Plan and organize your Torres del Paine park days: buy or confirm your CONAF park entrance pass online (required, ~$35 USD for international visitors). Review trail maps at the free park info center in town.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Puerto Natales' affordable restaurant strip. Enjoy a hearty local meal and rest early to prepare for the park.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — buy bread, eggs, and fruit from the supermarket (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from supermarket supplies along the waterfront (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: El Living Café or Afrigonia Restaurant in Puerto Natales — budget set menu (menú del día) typically ~$8-12 USD including soup, main, and drink

day_by_day.notes: Buying groceries today is essential for budget management throughout the trip. Park entrance fees must be paid — keep your receipt as rangers check it on trails. December is peak Patagonian summer so trails will be busy; start hikes early each day.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early shared bus or transfer from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine National Park (departs ~7:00-8:00 AM, ~$10-15 USD one way). Enter the park and head to the Laguna Amarga ranger station. Begin the Lago Nordenskjöld Shoreline Trek & Guanaco Spotting — trek along the vivid turquoise shores of Lago Nordenskjöld, one of the most scenic lakes in the park. The trail offers sweeping views of the Paine Massif reflected in electric-blue water. Keep eyes open for guanacos, Andean condors, and rheas grazing freely along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Lago Nordenskjöld shoreline trail at a relaxed pace, stopping frequently for photos and wildlife observation. The trail is relatively flat and accessible, ideal for acclimatizing legs after travel. Reach a scenic viewpoint for a packed lunch overlooking the lake. Return to the trailhead by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Natales via shared shuttle. Prepare tomorrow's packed lunch and gear. Rest and rehydrate.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departure (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch brought from Puerto Natales — sandwiches, fruit, nuts, energy bars (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or rice meal at accommodation kitchen (~$4-6 USD) or grab a cheap empanada dinner in town (~$5-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers — Patagonian weather changes rapidly even in summer. Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential at this latitude. Bring at least 2 liters of water per person. The park bus schedule is limited — confirm return times at the ranger station upon arrival. Wildlife is most active in early morning and late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 4:00 AM for the Mirador Base Las Torres Sunrise Hike — the crown jewel of Torres del Paine. Take the earliest shuttle into the park (~5:00 AM departure if available, or arrange a private transfer the night before). Begin the 4-5 hour hike from Hotel Las Torres trailhead. The trail climbs steeply through lenga beech forest and over a glacial moraine to reveal the iconic granite towers reflected in the turquoise lake below. Arrive at the base at sunrise for the most dramatic golden-pink light on the towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend time at the mirador (viewpoint) soaking in the breathtaking scenery. Begin the descent back to the trailhead (2.5-3 hours down). The descent offers different perspectives of the valley and surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Natales exhausted but exhilarated. Hot shower, stretching, and an early dinner. Legs will be tired — this is a strenuous 8-10 hour round trip.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed energy breakfast before 4:00 AM departure — oats, banana, peanut butter sandwich (~$2-3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the mirador — sandwiches, hard-boiled eggs, trail mix, chocolate (~$5-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself slightly — La Mesita Grande pizzeria in Puerto Natales offers good value wood-fired pizza (~$10-14 USD) — well deserved after this epic hike

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the trip. Start as early as humanly possible — both to catch sunrise and to beat crowds. The final moraine scramble is steep and requires careful footing. Trekking poles strongly recommended. Bring extra warm layers as the base is cold and windy even in December. This hike is approximately 19-22 km round trip with 800m elevation gain.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest day — take a slow morning. Do gentle stretching or yoga to recover legs from the Base Las Torres hike. Walk around Puerto Natales at a leisurely pace. Visit Patagonia Bookshop for free map browsing and trip planning. Organize and back up your best photos from the past days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Cueva del Milodón Natural Monument (accessible by local bus or hitchhiking, ~25 km from Puerto Natales). Explore the enormous prehistoric cave where remains of a giant ground sloth (Mylodon) were discovered. The surrounding landscape is dramatic and the site has a small free or low-cost museum. Walk the short nature trails around the cave — easy hiking with great views of the Torres del Paine massif in the distance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Natales. Visit a local peluquería (market stall) for fresh produce. Cook a budget feast at the hostel kitchen — Chilean cazuela stew or lentil soup.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — yogurt, granola, fruit at accommodation (~$3-4 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at Cueva del Milodón — leftovers, crackers, cheese, fruit (~$3-5 USD)
meals.dinner: Home-cooked meal at accommodation kitchen — lentil soup with bread (~$3-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are crucial on multi-day trekking trips to prevent injury. Use this time to wash clothes, recharge electronics, and refill supplies. Cueva del Milodón entrance fee is approximately $5,000-8,000 CLP (~$5-8 USD). Some travelers hitchhike to the cave — a common and generally safe practice in this region of Patagonia.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure into Torres del Paine for the Valle del Francés Condor Watching Trek — one of the most spectacular hikes in all of Patagonia. Take the morning catamaran or bus to Pudeto/Paine Grande area. Begin hiking into the Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers and dramatic granite walls. The trail ascends through southern beech forest with waterfalls cascading down from glaciers above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the valley to the Mirador Británico or Mirador Francés for panoramic views of the valley, hanging glaciers, and surrounding peaks including Cerro Paine Grande and Los Cuernos. Scan the skies carefully for Andean condors — with wingspans up to 3.2 meters, they are frequently spotted riding thermals above the valley walls. Begin descent in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Paine Grande or Pudeto and catch the late afternoon shuttle back to Puerto Natales. Dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Mirador Francés with jaw-dropping views — sandwiches, energy bars, dried fruit (~$5-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant in Puerto Natales — Restaurante El Asador for local lamb or beef stew (~$9-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Valle del Francés is part of the famous W Trek circuit. The catamaran across Lago Pehoé costs approximately $20-25 USD round trip but saves significant hiking time — budget for this. Alternatively, hike around the lake to save money but add 3-4 hours. Condors are most commonly spotted mid-morning when thermals develop. Bring binoculars if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning in Puerto Natales. Sleep in, do laundry, and reorganize gear. Visit the weekly local market if operating for fresh produce and local crafts at low prices. Spend time at a café with good wifi to update travel journals, contact family, and research the remaining days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided walk to Cerro Dorotea — a free hike just outside Puerto Natales (no park fees required). The 3-4 hour round trip hike through lenga beech forest leads to a panoramic viewpoint overlooking Puerto Natales, Seno Última Esperanza fjord, and on clear days, distant Patagonian peaks. A perfect low-key hike for tired legs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront — completely free and beautiful in December when daylight extends until 10:30 PM. Enjoy the long Patagonian summer evening light over the fjord.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs, toast, coffee (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Cheap local lunch spot — try a menú del día at a local comedor (set lunch) for soup, main course, and drink (~$6-9 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta dinner at accommodation (~$4-6 USD) — save money for upcoming days

day_by_day.notes: Cerro Dorotea trailhead is about 7 km from town center — walk, bike, or take a cheap local taxi. The hike is free and underrated by most tourists focused on the national park. December 21st is the summer solstice in the Southern Hemisphere — the longest day of the year, meaning extremely long daylight hours perfect for extended evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Torres del Paine for a full day exploring the Lago Grey sector — the western arm of the park. Take the morning bus to the Grey sector. Hike the Lago Grey trail from the Refugio Grey area along the lakeside. The lake is filled with massive floating icebergs calved from Glaciar Grey — an otherworldly blue-white spectacle. The shoreline trail (free with park pass) offers close-up views of icebergs and the glacier tongue in the distance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Lago Grey shoreline trail. Look for ice chunks washed ashore — some glow an ethereal electric blue from compressed ancient air bubbles. Wildlife including black-necked swans and Andean ducks are common on the lake margins. Optional: take the Lago Grey catamaran tour for closer glacier views (~$45-55 USD — a splurge but extraordinary; skip if strictly budget).
day_by_day.evening: Return shuttle to Puerto Natales. Relaxed evening, prepare for the next big hiking day.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Lago Grey shoreline among the icebergs — an unforgettable picnic setting (~$5-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget pizza or empanadas in Puerto Natales (~$7-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Lago Grey sector is less crowded than the Las Torres side — enjoy the relative solitude. The icebergs are completely safe to observe from shore but do not attempt to climb or swim near them. The glacier catamaran is a significant budget splurge — assess your remaining budget before booking. The bus to Grey sector is less frequent — confirm times at the Puerto Natales bus terminal the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Full day dedicated to the Mirador Los Cuernos hike — a stunning and less-crowded alternative viewpoint in the park. Take the morning bus to the park and hike the trail toward Los Cuernos (The Horns) — dramatic sedimentary-capped granite peaks that are among the most photographed formations in Patagonia. The trail winds along the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld with constant views of the Cuernos reflected in the turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the Mirador Los Cuernos for panoramic views. The area around Campamento Los Cuernos offers a peaceful rest stop. On the return, take a slightly different route along the lake shore to vary the scenery. Keep eyes open for guanacos, which are extremely common in this area and often approach hikers curiously.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Natales. Christmas Eve eve — pick up some local wine or craft beer for a small celebration at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch at Mirador Los Cuernos viewpoint (~$5-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at accommodation with local wine — pasta, canned tuna, vegetables (~$6-9 USD including wine)

day_by_day.notes: This trail is approximately 12-15 km round trip with moderate elevation gain. The Cuernos formation is most photogenic in morning and late afternoon light. Guanacos in this area are habituated to humans but maintain a respectful distance — do not feed them. Bring sun protection as the lakeside trail has minimal shade.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve — lighter activity day. Take a morning hike to the Salto Grande waterfall — one of the most accessible and impressive waterfalls in the park, where the turquoise waters of Lago Nordenskjöld thunder into Lago Pehoé. Short walk from the Pudeto area (free with park pass). The viewpoints offer spectacular photography opportunities with rainbow mist rising from the falls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mirador Pehoé viewpoint area — sweeping 360-degree views of the Paine Massif, Lago Pehoé, and the surrounding steppe. The area around Pudeto has several short interpretive trails. Spend the afternoon at a relaxed pace, absorbing the landscape and reflecting on the incredible week of hiking.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Natales for Christmas Eve. Join the local Nochebuena celebrations — Chilean Christmas Eve is a family-centered celebration. Many restaurants offer special Christmas menus. Enjoy the festive atmosphere of the small town.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered Christmas Eve breakfast — treat yourself to something special like pancakes (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Salto Grande — enjoy the waterfall soundtrack with your meal (~$5-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at a Puerto Natales restaurant — many offer set Nochebuena menus; budget approximately $15-20 USD for this celebratory meal

day_by_day.notes: Salto Grande is one of the most visited spots in the park — arrive early morning to beat the crowds. Christmas Eve (Nochebuena) is the main celebration in Chilean culture — expect restaurants to be busy, book ahead if possible. Some park services may have reduced hours around Christmas — check bus and shuttle schedules in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — rest and reflection morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront watching the Christmas morning light on the fjord. Many businesses will be closed today — a perfect excuse for a slow, restorative morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a final, gentle hike on the Sendero de Chile trail sections accessible near Puerto Natales — flat to moderate terrain through Patagonian steppe with views of the surrounding mountains. Perfect for a Christmas afternoon stroll. Look for the characteristic Patagonian wildlife: rheas (ñandú), guanacos, upland geese, and flamingos in the wetland areas near town.
day_by_day.evening: Final proper dinner in Puerto Natales. Celebrate the end of an incredible trekking adventure. Visit a local craft brewery if budget allows — Patagonia has a growing craft beer scene. Pack gear and organize luggage for departure.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast — visit a local café for coffee and medialunas (croissants) as a treat (~$4-7 USD)
meals.lunch: Self-catered picnic on the Sendero de Chile trail (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Puerto Natales restaurant — Patagonian lamb (cordero) is the regional specialty and worth trying as a Christmas splurge (~$15-20 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Chile is a public holiday — most shops, supermarkets, and many restaurants will be closed. Stock up on food and supplies on December 24th. The Patagonian cordero al palo (spit-roasted lamb) is a Christmas tradition in the region and one of the great culinary experiences of the trip — budget for this final special meal.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia. Wake early for one last sunrise walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront. Enjoy the morning light on Seno Última Esperanza fjord. Complete packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at accommodation if checkout is before transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, take a final short walk around Puerto Natales. Visit any last shops for souvenirs — look for local wool products, Patagonian crafts, and mate gourds as affordable authentic keepsakes. Head to the bus terminal or airport transfer point for onward journey to Punta Arenas airport.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Punta Arenas for onward flight. Reflect on 12 incredible days of hiking, trekking, and immersion in one of the world's most spectacular wilderness areas.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast or café breakfast in Puerto Natales (~$4-7 USD)
meals.lunch: Grab-and-go lunch from a bakery or supermarket for the road (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport food or meal in Punta Arenas depending on flight schedule (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm transfer or bus to Punta Arenas airport well in advance — book at least 2-3 days before departure. The bus journey from Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas takes approximately 3 hours. Allow at least 3-4 hours before your flight for the transfer. Patagonian weather can delay transport — build buffer time into your departure schedule. Declare any food items at customs if returning to the US. Take one last look at the mountains — you'll want to come back.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange pre-booked transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in Torres del Paine. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal or airport snack
meals.lunch: In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival — keep it simple after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to avoid delays at night. Confirm check-in details with Aegean Bliss Resort ahead of arrival. Pack a small carry-on snack bag for the journey. Hydrate well — Patagonia's dry air can be dehydrating.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Orient yourself with the park map, trail conditions, and ranger briefings available at the resort lobby. Pick up any last-minute gear or supplies from the resort shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle introductory walk along the Lago Nordenskjöld shoreline near the resort — a flat, accessible trail offering stunning turquoise lake views and a chance to spot guanacos grazing on the hillsides. This easy 2–3 hour stroll serves as a perfect acclimatization walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a warm shower. Head to the resort restaurant for a relaxed dinner. Review the upcoming W Trek plan, confirm bookings for refugios and guided experiences, and pack your day bag for tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fuel up with eggs, fresh bread, local cheeses, and fruit
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the resort or a light café meal at the resort — sandwiches, empanadas, and juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — try the Patagonian lamb stew (cazuela de cordero) or grilled salmon with local vegetables, mid-range pricing ~$25–35 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest and acclimatization day. Do not overexert yourself — Patagonia's wind and terrain can be demanding. Confirm W Trek refugio reservations and guided tour bookings. Weather in December can be unpredictable; check the park's official weather updates daily.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the iconic W Trek — Day 1 of the multi-day hike. Start with the Valle del Francés Condor Watching Trek. Depart early from the resort and take the catamaran across Lago Pehoé to Refugio Paine Grande. Begin the ascent into Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers and dramatic rock faces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking deeper into Valle del Francés toward Mirador Británico. Keep eyes skyward for Andean condors riding thermals above the valley walls. The round trip from Paine Grande is approximately 22 km — pace yourself and take breaks to absorb the breathtaking scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Refugio Paine Grande for the night. Enjoy a hot meal at the refugio dining hall. Share stories with fellow trekkers, dry gear, and rest well for the next day's leg of the W Trek.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — oatmeal, eggs, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — energy bars, nuts, dried fruit, cheese, and crackers (prepare the night before or purchase from resort)
meals.dinner: Hot dinner at Refugio Paine Grande — set menu typically includes soup, a main course of pasta or meat, and dessert (~$20–28 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book catamaran tickets across Lago Pehoé in advance — they fill up quickly in December (peak season). Refugio Paine Grande must be pre-booked. Bring trekking poles, wind layers, and rain gear. December days are long with up to 17 hours of daylight — great for extended hiking.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 2 — Trek west from Refugio Paine Grande toward Refugio Grey along the southern shore of Lago Grey. The 11 km trail offers dramatic views of the glacier-fed lake and the massive Grey Glacier in the distance. Spot floating icebergs drifting across the steel-blue water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Refugio Grey and drop your pack. Join the Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — paddle through icy turquoise waters surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. A guided 3–4 hour kayaking experience offering perspectives of the glacier impossible to see from land.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Refugio Grey for the night. Warm up with hot drinks and enjoy dinner at the refugio. Clean and dry your gear, treat any blisters, and rest your legs for the following day.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande — porridge, bread, jam, and coffee before hitting the trail
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten with glacier views — sandwiches, energy bars, and hot tea from a thermos
meals.dinner: Set dinner at Refugio Grey — hearty soup, main course, and dessert (~$22–30 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition must be pre-booked through the park concessionaire or your resort. Wear waterproof layers for kayaking — the glacier creates a cold microclimate. The trail between Paine Grande and Grey can be windy and exposed; secure all loose items on your pack.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 3 — Rest morning at Refugio Grey. Take a short optional hike to the Grey Glacier viewpoint for close-up views of the glacier face and ice formations. Photograph the stunning blue ice and listen for the thunderous crack of calving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek back east from Refugio Grey to Refugio Paine Grande (11 km), retracing the southern Lago Grey trail. The return journey offers new perspectives with the light shifting from the west. Arrive at Paine Grande and check in for a second night.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a well-deserved rest at Refugio Paine Grande. Attend an optional ranger talk about the park's ecology and conservation efforts, often held in the refugio common room in the evenings. Rest and prepare for the most iconic day of the trek.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Refugio Grey — eggs, toast, coffee, and fruit
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on the return trek — nuts, energy bars, dried mango, and a sandwich
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Paine Grande — enjoy the set menu with a glass of Chilean Carménère wine to celebrate the halfway point (~$25–35 USD including wine)

day_by_day.notes: This is a slightly shorter trekking day by design — a strategic rest before the demanding Las Torres hike on Day 7. Use the afternoon to air out boots, stretch, and mentally prepare. Confirm the catamaran schedule back to the resort for Day 6.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 4 — Take the morning catamaran from Refugio Paine Grande back across Lago Pehoé toward the eastern sector of the park. Transfer to the Las Torres sector and check into Refugio Las Torres or a nearby mid-range lodge for the night. Settle in and have lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lago Nordenskjöld Shoreline Trek & Guanaco Spotting — Trek along the vivid turquoise shores of Lago Nordenskjöld from the Las Torres sector. This scenic 3–4 hour moderate trek offers sweeping views of the Paine Massif reflected in the lake and excellent guanaco spotting opportunities along the grassy shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Refugio Las Torres. Lay out your gear for the pre-dawn start tomorrow. Set multiple alarms. Eat a hearty early dinner and be in bed by 20:00–21:00 to prepare for the 04:00 wake-up call.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande before the catamaran — bread, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Las Torres sector café or refugio — soup and a sandwich
meals.dinner: Early hearty dinner at Refugio Las Torres — pasta, protein, and plenty of carbohydrates to fuel tomorrow's big hike (~$20–28 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a critical logistics day. Confirm your early wake-up call with the refugio staff. Prepare your day pack the night before: headlamp, extra layers, snacks, water, camera, and trekking poles. The Mirador Base Las Torres hike requires an early 04:00–04:30 departure to reach the summit at sunrise.

day_by_day.morning: Mirador Base Las Torres Sunrise Hike — Wake at 04:00 and begin hiking by 04:30 under headlamp. The 4–5 hour round-trip trail climbs through lenga beech forest, exposed moraine fields, and boulder scrambles to reach the iconic granite tower base at sunrise. Arrive at the mirador as first light illuminates the three iconic granite spires reflected in the glacial lagoon below — one of the most spectacular sights in South America.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Refugio Las Torres, arriving by midday. Celebrate with a hot lunch and cold beer. Rest your legs, treat blisters, and enjoy the satisfaction of completing the W Trek's signature hike. Optional: soak feet in a cold stream near the refugio.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort by park shuttle or pre-arranged transfer. Arrive at the resort, enjoy a long hot shower, and treat yourself to a celebratory dinner at the resort restaurant. Reflect on the W Trek achievement.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed energy breakfast before the hike — banana, energy bar, and thermos of coffee consumed on the trail
meals.lunch: Hot lunch at Refugio Las Torres post-hike — burger, soup, or pasta with a well-deserved local beer (~$15–20 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — splurge slightly on the Patagonian lamb or king crab (centolla) if available (~$30–40 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire trip. Weather at the towers is highly variable — even in December, clouds can obscure the towers. If weather is poor, the refugio staff can advise on the best window. The sunrise timing in late December is approximately 05:30–06:00. Bring warm layers — the glacial lagoon creates a frigid microclimate at the base.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and spend the morning by the resort's beachfront area. Read, journal, or simply absorb the stunning Patagonian landscape from the comfort of the resort grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional gentle activity: take a short self-guided nature walk along the resort's immediate shoreline, birdwatching for Patagonian birds including the southern lapwing, black-necked swan, and Magellanic woodpecker. Alternatively, enjoy the resort's amenities — spa treatment if available, or simply relax.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset from the resort's beachfront — December sunsets in Patagonia occur around 22:00, offering extraordinary golden light over the lake and mountains. Have a quiet dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet — indulge in a slow, relaxed morning meal with fresh juice, pastries, eggs, and local cheeses
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café — salad, sandwich, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — try the Chilean cazuela (stew) or fresh trout with local herbs (~$25–35 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Do not underestimate the importance of this rest day after 5 consecutive days of trekking. Your body needs recovery before the remaining activities. Use this day to do laundry, recharge camera batteries, back up photos, and plan the final days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Lago Nordenskjöld Shoreline Trek & Guanaco Spotting (extended version) — Return to the Nordenskjöld shoreline for a longer, more exploratory version of the trek. Head out early when the light is golden and the guanacos are most active. Bring binoculars for wildlife spotting — look for Andean foxes, rheas (ñandú), and condors overhead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the shoreline trek to a more remote viewpoint for panoramic views of the Paine Massif. Enjoy a packed picnic lunch with one of the most spectacular mountain backdrops in the world. Return to the resort by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography session from the resort's beachfront — the late December light creates extraordinary conditions for landscape photography. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and early night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before heading out — eggs, toast, coffee, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch on the trail — artisan bread, local cheese, cured meats, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — grilled Patagonian lamb chops with chimichurri and roasted vegetables (~$28–38 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: December is peak guanaco season — females often have young calves (chulengos) at this time of year. Maintain a respectful distance of at least 30 meters from wildlife. The Nordenskjöld shoreline can be windy in the afternoon — start early to enjoy calmer morning conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve — Take a scenic morning drive or guided tour to the Salto Grande waterfall and Mirador Nordenskjöld viewpoint, two of the park's most accessible and dramatic landmarks. The waterfall connects Lago Nordenskjöld with Lago Pehoé in a thundering cascade of turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely afternoon. Optional: visit the park's visitor center to learn about the park's geology, flora, and fauna through interactive exhibits. Alternatively, take a short kayak or stand-up paddleboard session on the lake near the resort if available.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve celebration dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort. Many Patagonian resorts offer a special Christmas Eve set menu — expect Patagonian lamb, fresh seafood, and Chilean wines. Enjoy the festive atmosphere with fellow travelers under the long Patagonian twilight.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — enjoy a relaxed Christmas Eve morning meal
meals.lunch: Lunch at the park visitor center café or a packed lunch near Salto Grande — empanadas, juice, and snacks
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — splurge on the holiday set menu with wine pairing (~$50–70 USD per person, pre-book with the resort)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Christmas Eve dinner with the resort well in advance — it is likely to be a special event and may sell out. Salto Grande is one of the most visited spots in the park; arrive early in the morning to avoid crowds. The waterfall is most dramatic after recent rainfall.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — Celebrate with a sunrise walk on the resort's beachfront. Watch the early morning light transform the Paine Massif into shades of pink and gold. Enjoy a slow, festive Christmas breakfast at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final full adventure day: Valle del Francés Condor Watching Trek (day version from the eastern access). Take a park shuttle to the Francés valley trailhead and hike into the valley for condor watching and glacier views. This shorter day version allows you to experience the valley's grandeur without the full multi-day commitment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a final Christmas evening in Torres del Paine. Enjoy a sunset toast on the beachfront with a glass of Chilean sparkling wine (espumante). Farewell dinner at the resort, sharing memories of the trip with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Festive Christmas breakfast at the resort — special holiday spread with pastries, smoked salmon, eggs, and champagne mimosas
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch in Valle del Francés — festive treats including chocolate, nuts, dried fruits, and a thermos of hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — Patagonian lamb roast, Chilean wine, and dessert (~$40–55 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in the park is typically quieter than surrounding days — many visitors are resting. This makes it an ideal day for a final hike with fewer crowds on the trails. Condors are most active mid-morning when thermals begin to rise. Bring a telephoto lens or binoculars for the best condor viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake early for one last sunrise over the lake from the resort's beachfront. Take a slow farewell walk along the shoreline, absorbing the landscape one final time. Pack, check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, and arrange transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport. If time permits before departure, stop in Puerto Natales town for a final browse of local artisan shops — pick up Patagonian wool goods, locally made chocolates, or a bottle of Chilean wine as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Patagonia. Reflect on an extraordinary 12-day journey through one of the world's last great wilderness areas.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy every bite knowing it's the last morning in Patagonia
meals.lunch: Lunch in Puerto Natales town if schedule allows — try La Mesita Grande for pizza or Afrigonia for a creative Patagonian fusion meal (~$15–20 USD per person)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–4 hours for the transfer from Torres del Paine to Punta Arenas airport — roads can be slow and unpredictable. Confirm your flight details and transfer timing the night before. Patagonian customs regulations prohibit taking fresh food, seeds, or plant material out of the region — consume or discard any remaining trail food. Consider purchasing travel insurance that covers outdoor activities for future Patagonian adventures.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through the heart of Torres del Paine National Park. The trail covers approximately 80km and takes you through stunning valleys, glacial lakes, and dramatic granite towers. You'll pass through Valle del Francés, Mirador Las Torres, and the Grey Glacier, experiencing some of the most breathtaking scenery in all of Patagonia.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Base Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Wake before dawn and hike 4-5 hours to the iconic base of the Torres del Paine granite towers. Arriving at sunrise rewards you with golden light illuminating the three towering peaks reflected in the turquoise glacial lagoon below. This is arguably the most photographed and awe-inspiring viewpoint in all of Patagonia and a bucket-list moment for any nature lover.
experiences.location: Mirador Base Las Torres, Eastern Sector

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through icy turquoise waters surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. A guided kayaking tour brings you up close to the 6km-wide glacier face, offering a perspective impossible to achieve on foot. Expert guides provide all equipment and safety briefings, making this an accessible yet thrilling adventure for trekkers looking to diversify their Patagonian experience.

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Condor Watching Trek
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers and towering peaks including Paine Grande and Cerro Espada. This full-day trek is renowned for Andean condor sightings, with the massive birds riding thermal currents above the valley. The trail culminates at Mirador Británico, offering a 360-degree panorama of the park's most spectacular peaks.

experiences.name: Lago Nordenskjöld Shoreline Trek & Guanaco Spotting
experiences.description: Trek along the vivid turquoise shores of Lago Nordenskjöld, one of the most scenic lakes in the park, with the Paine Massif reflected in its glassy waters. This moderate trail is a prime location for spotting wild guanacos, Patagonian foxes, and rheas in their natural habitat. The route connects key sectors of the park and offers constantly changing perspectives of the iconic towers and horns above.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort awaits at arrivals. Enjoy a chilled welcome champagne in the vehicle during the scenic transfer to Torres del Paine. Check in to the Beachfront suite, receive a personalized orientation from the concierge, and settle in.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome tray prepared by the resort chef — artisan charcuterie, Patagonian lamb empanadas, local cheeses, and a selection of Chilean wines awaiting in-suite upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all hiking gear and layering clothes are accessible from luggage tonight. Resort concierge will brief you on the 12-day plan. Early rest is strongly recommended to prepare for the days ahead. Weather gear check with the resort guide is scheduled for early morning Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start with a private resort orientation walk along the beachfront lakeside trail. Meet your dedicated expert guide for a gear review and weather briefing. Explore the resort's immediate natural surroundings — spot local bird species including Andean condors circling overhead and guanacos grazing on the hillside. Light stretching and acclimatization yoga session offered by the resort on the deck overlooking the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided introductory nature walk along Lago Nordenskjöld's shoreline — a gentle 2-3 hour trek to ease into the Patagonian landscape. Your guide will introduce local flora, fauna, and geology. Stunning turquoise lake views with the Paine Massif as a backdrop. Return to resort for a hot stone spa treatment to prepare muscles for the trek-heavy days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's panoramic terrace as golden light bathes the granite towers. Private stargazing session with the resort's astronomer guide — Patagonia's remote skies offer extraordinary visibility.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet Patagonian breakfast at the resort restaurant — smoked salmon, avocado, local berry preserves, fresh-baked sourdough, eggs prepared to order, and freshly pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lakeside picnic curated by the resort chef — king crab salad, quinoa bowls, artisan bread, and chilled sparkling water with local herbs
meals.dinner: Five-course tasting menu at the resort's signature restaurant featuring Patagonian lamb slow-roasted over open fire, centolla (king crab) bisque, and a curated Chilean Carménère wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate acclimatization and orientation day. Patagonian weather can be extreme — use today to assess conditions and calibrate expectations with your guide. Confirm W Trek logistics and equipment list for Days 4–8.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 04:30 for the Mirador Base Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Private luxury vehicle transfers you to the trailhead. Begin the 4-5 hour guided ascent through lenga beech forest and dramatic boulder fields. Arrive at the iconic granite towers as the first light of dawn turns them a blazing amber and rose gold — one of Patagonia's most breathtaking spectacles. Your guide provides geological and ecological context throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend at a relaxed pace, pausing at scenic lookout points. Return to the resort by early afternoon. Enjoy a restorative hydrotherapy session at the resort spa followed by a private massage to aid muscle recovery.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the resort. Attend a private presentation by the resort's naturalist on the ecology of Torres del Paine National Park — preparation for the multi-day W Trek beginning tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike energy breakfast packed by the resort at 04:15 — thermos of specialty coffee, protein-rich granola pots, hard-boiled eggs, and energy bars
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch delivered in an insulated pack — smoked Patagonian trout sandwiches, fresh fruit, dark chocolate, and electrolyte drinks consumed at the tower base
meals.dinner: À la carte dinner at the resort — centolla risotto, wood-fired Patagonian lamb chops with chimichurri, and a classic Chilean Pisco Sour to celebrate the day's achievement

day_by_day.notes: This hike is strenuous (approximately 18–20 km round trip with 800m elevation gain). Trekking poles, layered clothing, and waterproof jackets are essential. Weather at the towers can shift rapidly — your guide carries emergency gear. Photography golden hour at the base is approximately 05:30–06:30 in December.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the iconic W Trek Multi-Day Hike — Day 1 of 5. After a hearty breakfast, your private guide and porter team depart from the resort with premium pre-packed gear. Trek the eastern arm of the W toward Mirador Las Torres via a different approach route, enjoying solitude away from day-trippers. Arrive at the luxury tented camp or premium refugio by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon exploration hike around the base camp area — your guide leads a focused wildlife walk spotting pumas (rare but possible), foxes, condors, and guanacos. Rest and acclimatize at camp.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the camp's elevated viewpoint. Campfire gathering with fellow trekkers (if any) or private fireside relaxation. Star identification session with your guide.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs, Patagonian cold cuts, fresh fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed trail lunch — focaccia sandwiches with roasted vegetables and local cheese, trail mix, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Premium refugio dinner or private chef-prepared camp dinner — hearty Patagonian stew, fresh bread, and Chilean red wine

day_by_day.notes: Luggage transfer service arranged — only carry a daypack with essentials. The resort coordinates all logistics with the W Trek premium camp operators. A private porter carries heavier supplies. Emergency satellite communication device carried by guide throughout.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 2 — Trek the central section toward Valle del Francés. Morning hike through pristine lenga beech forest with dramatic views of Lago Nordenskjöld shimmering below. The trail winds upward with increasing views of hanging glaciers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Valle del Francés Condor Watching Trek — ascend into the glacially carved valley. Your expert ornithologist guide identifies Andean condors riding thermals overhead with wingspans exceeding 3 meters. Observe hanging glaciers calving in real time with thunderous booms echoing through the valley. This is one of the most dramatic amphitheaters in all of Patagonia.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to the premium camp at Italiano or Británico. Hot shower at the premium refugio. Quiet evening journaling or reading with a glass of wine as the valley walls glow in twilight.

meals.breakfast: Hot camp breakfast — oatmeal with Patagonian berries, scrambled eggs, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at a scenic overlook — gourmet wraps, energy bars, nuts, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Refugio dinner with a premium upgrade — grilled chicken or vegetarian option with roasted vegetables, soup, and dessert; Chilean wine available

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is the crown jewel of the W Trek. Allow extra time at the condor-watching viewpoints — your guide will know the optimal positions. Wind can be extreme in the valley — secure all loose items and wear windproof layers.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 3 — Trek westward along the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld toward Paine Grande. The trail offers continuously spectacular lake and mountain panoramas. Spot guanacos grazing along the shoreline in large herds. Your guide shares insights into the lake's extraordinary turquoise coloration caused by glacial flour suspended in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Paine Grande lodge — the western hub of the W Trek. Rest, refresh, and enjoy the dramatic views of Grey Glacier from the lodge terrace. Optional short walk to a nearby viewpoint for the first glimpse of the Grey Glacier ice field.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of the glacier from the lodge terrace with a glass of Chilean sparkling wine. Communal or private dinner at the lodge. Briefing from your guide on tomorrow's kayaking expedition.

meals.breakfast: Hot camp breakfast — eggs, toast, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside trail lunch — Patagonian cheese and cold cuts on artisan bread, fresh fruit, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner — three-course meal featuring lake fish, roasted vegetables, and a dessert of calafate berry tart (the local Patagonian berry said to ensure your return)

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek is approximately 11 km and relatively moderate — a welcome relief before the glacier kayaking day. Lago Nordenskjöld's shoreline is one of the most photogenic sections of the entire W Trek. Bring extra memory cards for your camera.

day_by_day.morning: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — the most exclusive experience of the trip. After an early breakfast, don premium dry suits and safety gear provided by the expert guide team. Launch kayaks onto the milky turquoise waters of Lago Grey. Paddle through a surreal landscape of floating icebergs calved from the 270 km² Grey Glacier — one of the largest glaciers in Patagonia outside Antarctica.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the kayaking expedition closer to the glacier face. Marvel at the towering blue ice walls rising 30 meters above the water. Your guide explains glacial dynamics and climate change impacts. Return paddle to shore with the wind (ideally) at your back. Hot drinks and snacks at the kayaking base.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Paine Grande lodge. Premium spa treatment arranged at the lodge or private massage in your room. Celebratory dinner for completing the most adventurous day of the trip.

meals.breakfast: High-energy pre-kayak breakfast — eggs, avocado toast, granola, fresh juice, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Thermos of hot soup and gourmet sandwiches consumed on the kayak rest stop — a truly unforgettable al fresco dining experience surrounded by icebergs
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dinner — Patagonian king crab with butter and herbs, quinoa salad, and a celebratory bottle of Chilean Chardonnay

day_by_day.notes: Grey Glacier kayaking is weather-dependent — wind conditions on Lago Grey can be extreme. Your guide team will make a go/no-go decision each morning based on conditions. A backup activity (guided glacier viewpoint hike) is pre-arranged in case of cancellation. Dry suits keep you warm but movement is limited — listen carefully to the guide's paddling instructions.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 5 — Final day of the W Trek. Trek back along the southern shore of Lago Grey, enjoying a completely different perspective of the glacier and lake. The morning light on the ice field is spectacular. Your guide leads a final reflective walk, summarizing the ecological and geological highlights of the entire W Trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Boat transfer or private vehicle returns you from the western section of the park back to the Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrival at the resort — warm welcome from staff with hot towels and welcome drinks. Long hot shower, unpacking, and complete relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at the resort's finest table to mark the completion of the W Trek. Resort sommelier presents a curated wine flight to accompany the meal.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast — hot porridge, eggs, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Trail lunch en route — packed gourmet sandwiches and fruit consumed at a lakeside rest stop
meals.dinner: Grand celebration dinner at the resort — seven-course chef's tasting menu featuring the finest Patagonian ingredients: king crab, Patagonian lamb, wild mushrooms, and a dessert of calafate berry sorbet with champagne

day_by_day.notes: W Trek completion is a major achievement — 60–80 km over 5 days in one of the world's most dramatic landscapes. The resort team will have prepared a recovery kit in your room including Epsom salt bath products, muscle rub, and a selection of herbal teas.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day. Indulge in a 90-minute deep tissue massage at the resort spa followed by time in the hot tub overlooking the lake. Optional gentle yoga session on the beachfront deck at 09:00 led by the resort's wellness instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided photography walk along the resort's immediate shoreline — your guide positions you for the best light and composition for landscape photography. The afternoon light on the Paine Massif is extraordinary. Optional: private fly-fishing session on a nearby river with a licensed guide (gear provided).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour on the resort terrace. Private wine and cheese tasting curated by the resort sommelier — featuring premium Chilean and Argentinian wines paired with local Patagonian cheeses and charcuterie.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at the resort — full buffet spread with made-to-order omelets, smoked salmon, pastries, fresh fruit, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Light and restorative lunch at the resort — avocado and king crab salad, vegetable soup, and fresh-baked bread
meals.dinner: Intimate à la carte dinner — grilled Patagonian sea bass with herb butter, roasted root vegetables, and a classic crème brûlée for dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentional recovery day after the demanding W Trek. Resist the urge to over-schedule — your body needs rest before the final adventure days. The resort's spa team can design a personalized recovery program upon request.

day_by_day.morning: Lago Nordenskjöld Shoreline Trek & Guanaco Spotting — a refreshed and more leisurely version of this classic route now that your fitness is at its peak. Your private guide leads a 3-4 hour trek focusing on wildlife observation: guanaco herds, Andean foxes, flamingos at the lake's edge, and the ever-present condors. The turquoise lake against the granite towers is endlessly photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort. Afternoon at leisure — kayaking on the lake, paddleboarding, or simply reading on the beachfront with a glass of wine. Optional helicopter flightseeing tour over the park (weather permitting) — the ultimate aerial perspective of the glacier, towers, and lakes.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve celebration dinner at the resort — a special festive menu prepared by the executive chef. The resort decorates the dining room with a Patagonian-inspired holiday aesthetic. Fellow guests join for a communal Christmas Eve toast at midnight.

meals.breakfast: Christmas Eve brunch-style breakfast — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, fruit salad, and mimosas
meals.lunch: Lakeside picnic with holiday touches — festive hamper with cold cuts, cheeses, panettone, and sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve tasting menu — five courses celebrating Patagonian and Chilean cuisine with a festive twist; includes a welcome glass of Moët & Chandon Champagne for each guest

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve at Torres del Paine is magical — the long summer daylight means the sky remains light until nearly 22:00. The resort organizes a special bonfire on the beach with mulled wine and holiday music. Confirm helicopter tour booking at least 24 hours in advance due to weather dependency.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — begin with a private sunrise viewing from the resort's highest viewpoint, champagne in hand, as the first light of Christmas morning illuminates the Torres del Paine towers. Return to the resort for an extended festive breakfast celebration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final guided adventure — a private half-day trek to a lesser-known viewpoint in the park, away from all other tourists. Your guide reveals a hidden lagoon and waterfall accessible only with insider knowledge. This exclusive experience is the resort's gift to premium guests. Picnic lunch at the secret location.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Day farewell dinner — the resort's most elaborate meal of the trip. The executive chef prepares a grand Patagonian feast: whole-roasted Patagonian lamb (asado), king crab, fresh local vegetables, and a spectacular dessert spread. The resort sommelier presents a curated selection of premium Chilean wines. After dinner, gather around the outdoor fire pit for the final evening under Patagonia's extraordinary star-filled sky.

meals.breakfast: Grand Christmas breakfast feast — smoked salmon, eggs prepared every style, fresh pastries, holiday panettone, fruit platters, and unlimited sparkling wine and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Secret lagoon picnic — gourmet Christmas picnic hamper with cold Patagonian king crab, artisan bread, local cheeses, and chilled Chilean Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Grand Christmas asado feast — whole-roasted Patagonian lamb, king crab, grilled vegetables, traditional Chilean sides, and a dessert tower of calafate berry tart, chocolate mousse, and local ice cream; premium wine pairing throughout

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Patagonia is an experience unlike anywhere else on earth — summer solstice proximity means nearly 18 hours of daylight. The resort team works through the holiday to ensure an exceptional experience. Tip the staff generously — they are away from their families to make your Christmas unforgettable.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake at leisure for one last sunrise view from your beachfront suite. Pack and prepare for departure.
